analysis:
The supplied units are BASE-side text of scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py, an offline unittest that parses .github/workflows/ci.yml and the provider-ci-build composite action. The head-side text was not supplied, and the patch excerpt is truncated at about 3 KB. The changed ranges extend to head line 1007, so I could not see most of the new behavior. The visible patch hunk only adds test helper constants and functions: pinned checkout, cache restore and cache save SHAs, a SAVE_CACHES policy (pushes to master or dev only), a .git cache validation snippet, sparse-checkout patterns, and helpers for reading checkout options and work steps. These are test assertions only. They add no runtime provider, coordinator, or key-handling code. The base text shows no TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-011, TB-012 or TB-013 behavior, and it does not touch provider custody of A-003 or A-015. T-041 is the only cache threat supplied. It covers the provider's encrypted SSD prefix cache, which is unrelated to CI GitHub Actions cache.

The new CI behavior may add some attack surface. It restores and saves a shared .git directory cache across runs. It also restricts cache saves to pushes on master or dev, which is a cache-poisoning control, and it pins actions by SHA. I could not verify whether the actual workflow YAML matches those controls. Examples of what to check in the YAML: whether the .git cache can be written from pull-request contexts, whether a restored .git is validated, and whether secrets or tokens are exposed to PR-controlled code. The workflow and action files were not supplied, so I make no claim about them. Because the head side is unseen, I return no findings and flag a deeper review of ci.yml and the provider-ci-build action. This review is not a full audit.
